problem_statement: Nefa is the marketing site for a crypto exchange, built on this Nuxt 2 landing template. It has a home page (hero, live trending/gainers statistic cards, buy-and-trade, advanced trading tools, security, getting-started and FAQ sections), plus a /markets page and a /pricing page, all wrapped by a shared Navbar and Footer via the default layout. The growth team wants a single, consistent 'Market access ladder' rail that shows the four access tiers a customer can climb — Retail, Pro, Prime and Institutional, each with its headline coverage metric — so a visitor always sees the same access ladder no matter which marketing page they land on. In the navbar the team also wants a small tier picker: a 'Switch access tier' button next to an 'Access tier:' readout that names the tier the visitor is currently previewing, so the readout always reflects the live selection after a switch. Ship the access ladder so it (1) appears on the home, markets and pricing pages alike (rendered once from the shared layout, not pasted per page), (2) lays out its four tier tiles responsively without horizontal overflow on a phone, (3) matches the site's blue-gradient brand styling rather than an off-brand dark slab, and (4) keeps the navbar tier-picker readout in sync with the button so a visitor who switches tiers sees the readout name the new tier. Keep the rest of the site — navigation, hero, statistic cards, markets and pricing content and the static build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Market access ladder' rail so it renders on the home, markets and pricing pages (rendered once from the shared default layout, not a per-page copy).
The ladder shows a 'Market access ladder' label and four ordered tier tiles: Retail, Pro, Prime and Institutional, each with a coverage metric.
The tier tiles must wrap responsively so no marketing page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).
Style the ladder in the site's blue-gradient brand language (light card, blue accents), consistent and legible, not an off-brand dark slab.

Wire the navbar tier-picker so that after clicking 'Switch access tier', the 'Access tier:' readout names the newly selected tier (for example Pro) by reading the live selection, not a stale captured value.
Preserve the navigation, the hero, the statistic cards, the markets and pricing content, and the static Nuxt build with no console or network errors.
author_notes: Built on the RSurya99 nefa Nuxt 2 crypto-exchange landing template (shared Navbar/Footer via layouts/default.vue, data-driven trending/gainers statistic cards, Tailwind blue-gradient palette, AOS reveal). The shared Market access ladder and tier-picker are rendered with the local nefa logo and hero image assets already bundled under assets/img; no remote assets are added and the Poppins brand font is self-hosted. Design keywords: market access ladder rail, marketing continuity, crypto exchange tiers, brand palette, responsive layout.
design_constraints: Implement the Market access ladder as a shared component rendered from the default layout so a single source of truth reaches every marketing page; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.
The tier-tile row must use a fluid, wrapping responsive layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile; the tile spacing must stay legible.
The ladder must adopt the site's blue-gradient brand palette and card styling so it reads as part of Nefa, not a foreign dark block; keep it consistent with the marketing sections.
The navbar tier-picker readout must reflect the CURRENT selected tier after every switch by reading the live selection, so it can never go stale relative to the chosen tier.
Do not remove or regress the navigation, the hero, the statistic cards, the markets/pricing content, the local image assets or the static build.

change_completion: The Market access ladder is present on the home, markets and pricing pages (the shared component reaches all three routes).

After clicking the navbar 'Switch access tier' button on the home page, the 'Access tier:' readout updates to name the newly selected tier (for example Pro) — the post-interaction terminal state changed from the initial selection.
design_consistency: The ladder on the home states matches the reference's blue-gradient brand styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not an off-brand dark slab.
The ladder adopts the site's blue-accent card idiom so it reads as part of Nefa across the marketing pages.
responsive: No captured marketing page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the tier-tile row wraps.
mobile_initial, mobile_ladder_home and mobile_markets keep the layout readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: Navigation (home/markets/pricing), the navbar and footer remain present and functional.
The existing hero, statistic cards, markets and pricing content and the static Nuxt build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the rebranded homepage hero and responsive shell.
desktop_markets and desktop_pricing protect the secondary marketing pages and must carry the Market access ladder.
mobile_markets and mobile_pricing protect the secondary pages across viewports without horizontal overflow.
desktop_ladder_home and mobile_ladder_home scroll the Market access ladder into view and must show the blue-accent ladder without horizontal overflow.
toggle_tier_home clicks the navbar tier-picker; the 'Access tier:' readout must then name the newly selected tier.
